chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Mi'za, from al-Halabi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who acknowledged a debt to an heir while in his illness; is that permissible? He said, 'Yes, if he is wealthy.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a dying person to acknowledge a debt to one specific heir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a dying person's acknowledgment of a debt to a specific heir is valid provided the debtor is solvent (*maliyyan*), ensuring the debt is genuine rather than a mechanism to artificially inflate one heir's share. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of verifying the authenticity of debts during the *marad al-mawt* (illness of death) to prevent unjust distribution of the estate. It highlights the balance between respecting the deceased's final declarations and protecting the equitable rights of all heirs.
